summary: In a predawn rainforest setting, the narrator tries to revive Steve, who has been sedated and bruised, by slapping him, walking him to a window, and talking to him until his eyes focus. He asks about her first, and she hugs him while privately worrying that Ramos may kill them both now that Alex Goddard has gotten what he wanted. The narrator reflects that the ancient forest still holds horror, unlike the fairy-tale woods of the past. The passage is an excerpt from a thriller, 'Book 3 — part 177'.
one_line: In a predawn rainforest, the narrator works to revive a drugged, bruised Steve while fearing Ramos's next move.
key_facts: The narrator says that in an ancient rainforest all things are still possible.
The narrator notes that old fairy tales took place in a deep wood where evil could lurk unfettered.
The narrator, Steve, and Sarah are marooned in a thousand-year-old forest where horror still lived.
Steve is wearing a shift, and his clothes hang from a hook on the door.
The narrator stares at bruises on Steve's face and asks, 'God, baby, what did he do to you?'
The narrator pulls Steve's feet out of the bed onto the linoleum floor and drags him to the slatted window at the rear of the room.
It takes ten minutes of working on Steve before his eyelids begin to flutter.
Steve's timorous voice asks, 'Can I please lie down?'
The narrator tells Steve, 'Baby, just walk a little more' to flush the chemicals out of his brain.
Steve's first question is 'Morgy, are you okay?' and he asks about her before anything else.
Steve grins with only half his face, and the narrator can tell even that hurts.
The narrator wonders whether Ramos will kill them both now that Alex Goddard has gotten everything he wanted.
The narrator decides not to share the possibility of being killed with Steve at this moment.
